chief_complaint: chronic foul-smelling ear drainage and attic keratin mass
hpi_details: 35-year-old male presents with a 2-year history of chronic, painless, foul-smelling purulent drainage from his left ear, accompanied by progressive conductive hearing loss. He has a history of recurrent otitis media as a child.
ideas: thinks it might be related to cholesteatoma
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan
pmh: History of recurrent otitis media as a child

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Cholesteatoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes prompt ENT referral for surgical tympanomastoidectomy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: chronic foul-smelling ear drainage and attic keratin mass

Key HPI features: A 35-year-old male presents to the clinic with chronic foul-smelling ear drainage and attic keratin mass. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Cholesteatoma.
Relevant background/PMH: History of recurrent otitis media as a child
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Cholesteatoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Chronic otitis externa without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Dizziness or facial weakness.
management_principles: Plan for Cholesteatoma: Refer to ENT for surgical tympanomastoidectomy
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 35M presenting with chronic, painless, malodorous left otorrhea and ipsilateral hearing loss.
reference_soap.objective: Otoscopy reveals a retracted tympanic membrane with a pearly white keratinized mass/debris in the pars flaccida (attic) region of the left ear. Purulent discharge noted. Tuning fork test confirms conductive hearing loss on the left (Weber lateralizes to left, BC > AC).
reference_soap.assessment: Cholesteatoma of the left middle ear.
reference_soap.plan: ENT referral for surgical excision (tympanomastoidectomy) to prevent potentially lethal complications (e.g., bony destruction, facial nerve palsy, intracranial abscess). Water precautions.

Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Cholesteatoma
Implement evidence-based management plan: Refer to ENT for surgical tympanomastoidectomy
